title: Current, voltage and AC/DC
blurb: Name the unit for each electrical quantity, tell conductors from insulators, and explain what makes AC different from DC.

T5A01.why: Current is the flow of charge, measured in **amperes**.
T5A01.trap: Volts measure the push, ohms the opposition, watts the power.

T5A02.trap: Watt-hours are energy (power over time), not power itself.

T5A03.why: Electrons flowing through a circuit is **current**.
T5A03.trap: Voltage is the push that causes flow, not the flow.

T5A04.trap: Wavelength is distance per cycle, not cycles per second.

T5A05.why: Electrons move when there is a difference in **voltage** between two points: the push.
T5A05.trap: Capacitance and inductance store energy; they don't start the flow.

T5A06.why: Frequency is measured in **hertz**: cycles per second.
T5A06.trap: Henry is inductance, farad is capacitance.

T5A07.why: Metals have many **free electrons** that drift when voltage is applied.
T5A07.trap: Electrons carry current, not protons. Density has nothing to do with it.

T5A08.why: **Glass** holds its electrons tightly, so it insulates. Sea water, stainless steel and graphite all conduct.

T5A09.why: AC alternates between **positive and negative** directions, swinging through zero each time.
T5A09.trap: Swinging only to zero and back is pulsing, not AC.

T5A10.why: The rate at which electrical energy is used is **power**.
T5A10.trap: Current is flow and voltage is push. Neither one is a rate of energy use.

T5A11.why: Resistance opposes any current: **DC, AC and RF** alike.
